discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases, mesoscopic quantum transport)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can drive a time-reversal-invariant insulator into a new state of matter, the quantum spin Hall phase, classified by a Z2 topological invariant. They generalised the idea to three dimensions and to topological superconducting proximity effects. In 2007 Molenkamp's group observed quantised edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells, confirming the first topological insulator and following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. This work established topology as an organising principle for band structures, and it gave rise to a large field: three-dimensional topological insulators, Weyl semimetals, topological superconductivity and routes to protected qubits. The ideas are deep and have been tested precisely in mesoscopic transport experiments, including helical edge states, nonlocal transport and 4π-periodic Josephson effects in HgTe junctions. They unify band theory, symmetry and quantum coherence, and they remain central to the second quantum revolution.
